https://www.leaderlive.co.uk/news/nation.text: Do not cancel travel plans over wildfires, urges French minister By PA News Agency Share 0 Comments 3 Skip to next photo 1 / 1 Show caption 1 / 1 Share 0 Comments This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A French foreign minister has urged tourists not to cancel their travel plans despite unprecedented wildfires in the country’s south west. Éléonore Caroit, the minister for international partnerships, said that although France was facing an “exceptionally intense” fire season, tourists should visit as long as they remain well-informed. Massive forest fires have forced the evacuation of 200,000 people in south-western France and central Spain, including 141,000 in the Gironde and Landes departments in France. Ms Caroit told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme on Saturday: “It’s more than an incident, it really is a tragedy, nearly 50,000 hectares have been burned this year. It’s significantly worse than last year and even 2022, which was the worst year we had had. “You have entire areas that are fine, you’re seeing similar phenomena in Spain and other countries. I’m in Paris and nothing is happening, and most other regions are OK, so do please come to France and do not cancel your travel plans. “But wherever you are, please do be advised as to what might be happening.” Ms Caroit, who said the French army had been deployed to help tackle the wildfires which now number 32, also told the programme that France’s response was being bolstered by their European Union membership. A water bomber fighting wildfires In Ares, western France (Caroline Blumberg/AP) She said: “Being part of the European Union today makes every possible sense. We have activated the European Civil Protection Mechanism which is an extraordinary mechanism; solidarity is essential in the EU. “Right now, we have had the confirmation that two water bombing carriers will come from Croatia, two water tractors from Portugal, two Black Hawk helicopters from Czech Republic and Slovakia. “They’re helping us now as the situation is terrible; we’ve helped them in the past. It explains what it is to be in the EU.” Ms Caroit urged world leaders to see the fires – which have killed two firefighters, injured 42 more and are confirmed to have destroyed around 100 homes so far – as a wake-up call for climate change. A wildfire advances near San Martin de Valdeiglesias, Ávila province, Spain (Manu Fernandez/AP) She said: “(This is) something we’re seeing in many parts of the world. Remember the wildfires in California, Chile. The climate is changing, we’re having a terrible impact on it. “While leaders in the world continue to say climate change doesn’t matter, we’re seeing the concrete effects everywhere. We have to take it seriously. “(France has) invested millions but we’re seeing it’s not enough.” Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said: “My thoughts are with everyone affected by the wildfires in Europe. “I am in touch with my French and Spanish counterparts about the situation. “British nationals should follow the advice of local authorities in the area, alongside FCDO travel advice.” A British restaurant owner in Bordeaux said the city is “full of smoke and ash” and residents are wearing masks if they go outside. Lance Attwood, 58, who owns Sweeney Todd’s in Bordeaux city centre, told the Press Association: “It’s not really conducive to coming out. “The town is full of smoke and ash, so there’s a big drop in business, people are just walking around town in masks. “Our biggest concern is people’s safety and the safety of the emergency services.” Mr Attwood, who has lived in Bordeaux for 25 years, said friends who had been evacuated were focusing on recovering sentimental belongings and finding alternative living arrangements. He encouraged people to donate dry food with a long shelf-life to local charities to help those affected. Share 0 Comments Get involved with the news Send your news & photos Loading... https://www.dw.com/en/several-killed-in-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5LvRF The Federal Aviation Administration said Prime Air Flight 7598 overran the runway while landing around 2 p.m. local time Image: Joe Raedle/Getty Images/AFP Advertisement An Amazon cargo plane barreled off a runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday, killing at least five people as it struck vehicles and burst into flames, authorities said. The aircraft overran the runway around 2 p.m. local time, or 18:00 GMT, after arriving from San Juan, Puerto Rico. Five people were killed, three critically injured and two others hospitalized with less severe injuries, Miami-Dade County officials said at a press conference. "Right now, our absolute priority is the safety, well-being and care of everyone involved. We’re doing everything we can to support those affected," officials said, adding that it was too soon to determine whether those killed were on the plane or in vehicles struck by the aircraft. According to the authorities, the crash sent thick black smoke billowing into the sky and trapped the pilot and copilot in the cockpit, as well as some people in cars. Investigation launched into cause of crash The Prime Air aircraft appeared to be resting on its belly and was largely intact despite the fire. The NTSB said in an X post on Sunday the B-767-300 cargo airplane was flying into Miami from San Juan, Puerto Rico and they have "launched a go team to investigate Sunday's runway excursion accident." The flight was operated by 21 Air, a North Carolina-based cargo carrier. The 32-year-old Boeing 767 was originally built to carry passengers and flew for several airlines before being converted to a cargo plane in 2015, according to Flightradar24. Amazon said it would cooperate with the investigation. The National Transportation Safety Board said it was sending a team to Miami to investigate. Amazon said it would cooperate with the investigation Image: Marco Bello/REUTERS “We’re heartbroken to learn that five people lost their lives in today’s incident at Miami International Airport,” the company said in a statement. “Our deepest sympathies go out to the families, loved ones and all those affected by this devastating loss." About 250 flights were delayed at the airport by late Sunday afternoon, according to FlightAware. Fire crews were still dealing with a fuel leak several hours later, according to reports. Eyewitness say they saw 'thick black smoke billowing into the sky' Jackson Lee, who runs an electronics shop near the crash site, told news agencies that he went outside with four colleagues after the crash and saw smoke rising near the airport’s fences. "We hear planes taking off and landing every five minutes. I thought I’d got used to it," Lee said. "I never thought it could come this close to us."
